title: Database defense-in-depth and lock/quota invariants are incomplete

original_titles.title: Reads do not use read-only sessions with a short statement timeout
No PostgreSQL RLS as defense in depth
No PostgreSQL row-level security behind the app layer (PMX-04 S3)
Lock order deviates (progress pointer locked before stage row); caps via COUNT without quota-row FOR UPDATE
Root-cause group is not the award unit; one group can be paid multiple times

problem: App-level tenant checks are not yet implemented everywhere, PostgreSQL RLS is absent, read sessions lack explicit read-only/short statement timeouts, and some counters/locks rely on COUNT queries rather than a dedicated quota row. gt_admin appears to have broader schema grants than a pure evaluator needs. Some award uniqueness semantics differ from the spec.
impact: A missed app authorization check or unexpected transaction can bypass intended isolation; lock contention and concurrent cap enforcement may behave differently under burst traffic.

verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: First finish tenant_id propagation and explicit event scope checks; RLS is defense in depth, not a substitute for application authorization.
Add PostgreSQL RLS policies for tenant-scoped app tables and set an unforgeable transaction-local tenant context. Ensure worker/admin bypass roles are intentionally separate.
Split DB roles by service: participant API, admin API, evaluator read-only GT, authoring GT write, worker app operations. Revoke unused schema/table rights.
Use read-only transactions and statement_timeout for read-heavy endpoints; define lock ordering for event/stage/team/progress/ledger rows.
Replace COUNT-only quotas with a locked quota/counter row or atomic conditional update; add high-concurrency cap/award tests.

acceptance_criteria: RLS policies prevent cross-tenant reads even when a route query omits tenant predicate.
Least-privilege grants are tested in PostgreSQL.
Concurrent submissions cannot exceed caps or double-claim awards.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.
